courses.subject: CJA
courses.title: Science-Based Interviewing
courses.description: This interactive course introduces students to science-based interviewing techniques grounded in empirical research and current legal standards. Utilizing adult-learning methodologies-including lecture, facilitation, audio/visual aids, and practical exercises-students will learn how to conduct interviews that produce reliable, accurate information. The course contrasts evidence-based practices with outdated methods historically linked to unreliable statements and false confessions. Emphasis is placed on compliance with AB 2644, including the prohibition of pseudo-scientific techniques and psychological coercion, regardless of the interviewee's age. This course is designed for criminal justice professionals seeking to improve investigative outcomes through lawful and ethical interview practices. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only.

courses.subject: CJA
courses.title: Campus Law Enforcement Update
courses.description: This course is designed to expand the knowledge of peace officers working a campus environment. The course will include a history of campus law enforcement, legal authority, laws and liability, responsibility in learning environment, campus conduct, emergency response tactics, and the discipline process as it relates to students. courses.subject: CJA
courses.title: Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) Block 1
courses.description: Block 1 of the Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) introduces first-line and mid-level law enforcement leaders to the principles of adaptive leadership, self-awareness, and professional purpose. Through guided discussion, group exercises, case studies, and reflective practice, participants examine personal values, leadership paradigms, accountability, and meaning in service. The course emphasizes the foundation of ethical leadership, the development of reflective habits, and the initiation of a personal adaptive leadership project. This course is one of eight SLI courses; completion of all eight (CJA 091A-091H) is required to earn the Certificate of Achievement. Designed for POST Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) cohorts. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only.
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: CJA
courses.title: Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) Block 2
courses.description: Block 2 of the Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) advances first-line and mid-level law enforcement leaders in adaptive leadership, ethical decision-making, resilience, and reflective practice. Through guided case studies, films, seminars, and leadership journals, participants analyze complex organizational challenges, apply adaptive leadership tools, and develop personal leadership artifacts. Topics include emotional survival and wellness, virtue ethics, adaptive leadership in action, followership, and team culture. This course is one of eight SLI courses; completion of all eight (CJA 091A-091H) is required to earn the Certificate of Achievement. Designed for POST Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) cohorts. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only.

courses.title: Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) Block 3
courses.description: Block 3 of the Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) continues the professional development of law enforcement supervisors through the exploration of ethical reasoning, values-based decision-making, and the dynamics of followership and leadership accountability. courses.title: Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) Block 4
courses.description: Block 4 of the Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) advances law enforcement supervisors' leadership skills through the applied study of communication, team dynamics, and organizational change. Participants analyze common barriers to effective team performance, practice effective presentation and active listening techniques, and explore strategies for principled policing and adaptive leadership. Through team projects, case studies, and reflection, students strengthen their ability to lead functional teams, facilitate dialogue, and manage change within complex law enforcement environments. This course is one of eight SLI courses; completion of all eight (CJA 091A-091H) is required to earn the Certificate of Achievement. Designed for POST Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) cohorts. courses.title: Supervisory Leadership Institute (SLI) Block 5

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
